clues: A megacity packs seven old islands, now joined into one, along a narrow coastal strip facing a wide western sea, with forested hills behind.
One summer monsoon dumps most of the year's rain in about four months — streets can flood waist-deep — then eight dry months follow.
Handed over as a royal dowry in 1661, it grew from trading port to mill town to the commercial heart of its subcontinent by 1900.
Its film studios release more movies per year than any other city on earth, and its lunch couriers deliver two hundred thousand home-cooked meals a day.
The triumphal stone arch on the waterfront, built for a visiting king, still frames the old harbor.
